la:adj:mas.html:
mās, măris (n. mare, rare;
gen. plur

marium, ; ), adj.

prob. from Sanscr. root man, think; manus, man, human being; cf.: memini, moneo, etc.
, male, masculine, of the male sex: mare et femineum sexus,: maribus (sc. diis),: si marem (anguem) emisisset ... si feminam, etc.,; ; so, emissio maris anguis (opp. emissio feminae anguis),: mas vitellus, a male yolk, i. e. which would produce a male chick, .—Of plants: ure mares oleas,.—

Transf., masculine, manly, brave (poet.): quod mares homines amant,: maribus Curiis,: animi,: male mas,unmanly, effeminate,: atque marem strepitum fidis intendisse Latinae,i. e. a manly, noble strain,.—As subst.: mās, măris, a male (opp. femina, v.infra).
Lit., of gods, human beings, and animals: congressio maris et feminae,: et mares deos et feminas esse dicitis,: (bestiarum) aliae mares, aliae feminae sunt ... et in mare et in femina, etc.,; cf.: feminaque ut maribus conjungi possit,: marium expers,; so, marium pignora, Oud. N. cr.: stuprum in maribus,: vos tollite laudibus, mares, Delon Apollinis,.—
Trop., of plants: in tilia mas et femina differunt omni modo: namque et materies dura ac nodosa, etc.,: cognati virilis sexus, per mares descendentes,.

la:adj:Massicus.html:
Massĭcus, i, m. (with or without mons),
a mountain in Campania, celebrated for its excellent wine, now Monte Massico: per juga Massici montis,: vertunt felicia Baccho Massica qui rastris (sc. juga, or arbusta),: in Massici radices,.—Hence, Massĭcum vīnum, or simply Mas-sĭcum, i, n., wine of the Massicus, Massic wine: veteris pocula Massici,; : vina,: Bacchi umor,; .

massa, ae, f., = μάζα,
that which adheres together like dough, a lump, mass (poet. and post-Aug.): massa picis,: salis,: lactis coacti,cheese,: lactis alligati,.—Of metals: versantque tenaci forcipe massam,: aeris,: chalybis,: ardens,.—Of money: tum argenti montis, non massas habet: Aetna non aeque altast,.— Absol., of a mass of gold: contactu gleba potenti Massa fit,: marmoris, a block of marble: marmor, non in columnis crustisve, sed in massa,.—Of chaos, .—Of a heavy weight, .—Of an indeterminate quantity of land, .

la:adj:masculinus.html:
mascŭlīnus, a, um, adj.
masculus
,
male, masculine; of human beings, animals, and plants (not in Cic.; perh. not ante-Aug.).
Lit.: membra,the male parts,: facies,: rapa rotunda masculini sexus,.—
Transf.
(Cf. masculus, II. B.) Manly, worthy of manhood: masculini viri, v. l. ; al. leg. masculi.—
In gram., of gender, masculine: masculina Graeca nomina,: ut si quaeratur, funis masculinum sit an femininum,: masculino genere cor enuntiavit Ennius, Caesell. Vindex ap. .—Hence, adv. (post-class.).
mascŭlīnē, in the masculine gender, : masculine etiam dicebant frontem, Paul. ex Müll.: caelum masculine veteres dixerunt, P. —*
mascŭlīnĭter, in the masculine gender, Vet. Interpr. Iren. 1, 1.

senses: Used of the larger and coarser varieties of plants or other natural products
la:adj:masculus.html:
mascŭlus, a, um,
adj. dim. [mas], male, masculine; subst., a male (not in Cic. or Cæs.).
Lit.: bona femina, et malus masculus,: incertus infans natus masculus an femina esset,: genus,: genus masculum femininumve,: tura,; Ov. Med. fac. 94; : dare mascula nomina rebus,: libido, i. e. tribadum,.—
Transf.
Of things: cardo, which is inserted into another (opp. cardo femina, into which another is inserted), ; v. cardo; of gems,.—
Worthy of or befitting a man, manly, vigorous, bold: proles,: Sappho,: animus,: ingenium, , p. 190, 25: indicium masculi et incorrupti viri,; v. masculinus.

la:other:Massilia.html:
Massĭlĭa, ae, f., = Μασσαλία,
a celebrated seaport town in Gallia Narbonensis, a colony from Phocæa, and a seat of Greekcivilization, now Marseilles, ; cf. ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—Hence,
Massĭlĭānus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Massilia, Massilian: vinum,in lemm.—
Mas-sĭlĭensis, e, adj., of or belonging to Massilia, Massilian: mores,i. e. Sybaritic, luxurious,.—In plur. subst.: Massĭlĭenses, ĭum, m., the inhabitants of Massilia, Massilians, ; ; et saep.; transf. for Massilia,.—
Massĭlĭōtĭcus or Massălĭōtĭcus (acc. to the Gr. Μασσαλιωτικός), a, um, adj., of or belonging to Massilia, Massiliotic: ostium Rhodani,; .—
Massī^lītānus, a, um, adj., Massilitan; in tmesi: Massili portabant juvenes ad litora tanas, Enn. ap. P. (Ann. v. 605 Vahl.).—Subst.: Massī^lītāni, ōrum, m., the Massilians, .—
Massĭlĭtānum, i, n., wine of Massilia, in lemm.
